newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dublin's Bruton backs N.Ireland talks timetable.
newsitem.headline: Dublin's Bruton backs N.Ireland talks timetable.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Monday that Northern Ireland's stalled peace talks should aim for progress under a fixed timetable after the British election is over.
The negotiations are due to be suspended later this week in the run-up to the election that British leader John Major must call by May.

Bruton, speaking to a meeting of British and Irish parliamentarians, said: "I believe that when the talks resume, it will be important that significant progress is made within a finite period, in order to steer negotiations through to success as speedily as possible.
"A timeframe and a calendar agreed among the participants for the conduct of negotiations would be a sensible and worthwhile way to achieve that."

He attacked hardline Irish Republicans for what he called their "self-imposed exclusion" from the talks due to the Irish Republican Army's continued guerrilla campaign to oust Britain from Northern Ireland.
Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, has been barred from the talks until the guerrillas agree to call another ceasefire.

"Sinn Fein are not there because of the return to violence by the IRA and that will remain the situation unless the ceasefire is unequivocally, believably and genuinely restored," Bruton told the 50 lawmakers from either side of the Irish Sea.

Calling for compromise from the province's Protestant majority and the Irish nationalist Catholic minority, Bruton said: ""Both sides need to accept the principle of consent and both sides need to abandon the option of coercion."
